Welcome to Granville Plus Nursery
Headteacher - Fiona Gaughan
Welcome to Granville Plus Nursery School, I am very proud to be the Headteacher.
We are a Maintained Nursery School that offers provision for children aged 6 months to 4 years planned and led by qualified teachers.
We are committed to fostering a LOVE OF LEARNING in every child. Our nurturing environment ensures that your little ones not only learn but also have fun and feel safe. We believe that the early years are crucial for development, and our dedicated team works hard to create a warm, welcoming space where your child can thrive. Our Curriculum is designed around the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), which supports all aspects of learning. This approach ensure a well-rounded experience , preparing your children not just for school, but for life. At Granville Plus Nursery School, we tailor learning experiences to suit individual needs, helping each child to reach their full potential.
We understand that choosing the right nursery is a big decision for parents. That's why we invite you to visit Granville and see for yourself. Please contact Cecilia on 020 7604 4620 to arrange a time.
Together, we are growing the leaders of tomorrow, one curious mind at a time.

Equal Opportunities - Equality Statement
We actively promote equal opportunities and race equality at the School. All children, parents, carers and staff are valued and respected as individuals, irrespective of their race, culture, class, gender, religion or age. We welcome the diversity of culture and experience we have at Granville Plus, not least for the contribution it makes to learning. We feel we can learn from the children and their families, from experience and from colleagues. Everyone is enriched by learning about eachothers’ backgrounds.
We know that to be a successful learner your child needs a positive self-image. Children need to feel that they belong and that they have responsibilities as part of the group, and as individuals.
Our resources and activities aim to reflect the diversity of children’s experiences and cultures. We encourage and respect children in the use of their first language and culture.
Hurtful remarks or actions, name calling, racist or sexist comments are not acceptable. Staff will discuss these issues with the children as they arise. We will also challenge any discriminatory or derogatory remarks or behaviour in adults.
Equality Information
The Equality Act 2010 has replaced all previous equality information such as the Race Relations Act, Disability Discrimination Act and Sex Discrimination Act. It was introduced to ensure protection from discrimination, harassment and victimisation on the grounds of "protected characteristics". This means that schools cannot discriminate against pupils or treat them less favourably because of their race, disability, religion or belief, gender reassignment, sexual orientation or pregnancy or maternity.
The Equality Act requires all schools to comply with the Public Sector Equality Duty, and two "specific duties".
The Public Sector Equality Duty requires us to:
Eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation, advance equality of opportunity between different groups, and foster good relations between different groups.
The two "specific duties" require us to:
We recognise that these duties reflect international human rights standards as expressed in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, the UN Convention on the Rights of People with Disabilities, and the Human Rights Act 1998.
We are a Bronze Level Unicef Rights Respecting School.

Exploring, Creating and Learning together at Granville
Granville Plus Nursery School is currently undergoing exciting building works which, once completed, will further enhance our provision with new spaces and resources for children and families. In the meantime, our two-year -old provision and nursery classes are learning together in a shared environment. This has many benefits in line with the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS): younger children learn by watching and imitating older children, while older children develop confidence, independence and empathy by supporting the younger ones. At times, our babies also join in and experience this provision, fully supported by their familiar adult.
Staff plan experiences carefully to meet the needs of each age group, ensuring that all children continue to thrive, build strong social skills and make progress.
Learning Through Play
We know that PLAY is how children learn BEST. Through play, children make friends, learn to share and take turns, building confidence, and discover new ideas. They explore, problem-solve, and use their imagination, all while developing key skills for life and future learning.
PLAY really is children's work - and it is how they LEARN, GROWN AND THRIVE.
Our children have been busy learning, exploring, and discovering new things every day! Take a look at some of their wonderful achievements. We may well have the artists, builders, and inventors of the future right here!
/i/video/e63db16f-773d-4a43-8cd3-dfbdb6d01b4c__1_.mp4
Stories and Themes at Granville Plus Nursery School
This term, the children have been busy exploring lots of exciting stories and themes! We loved celebrating Black History Month, sharing books that celebrate diversity, kindness, and community. The children enjoyed talking about the stories, learning about inspiring people, and taking part in creative activities linked to the themes.
We’ve also been reading the much-loved story Owl Babies by Martin Waddell. The children have been retelling the story in their own words and talking about how the baby owls felt — helping them to build empathy, understanding, and rich language.
Through these experiences, the children have been developing their confidence, imagination, and communication skills — all while having lots of fun learning together!

INCLUSION, SEND AND LOCAL OFFER
SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS AND DISABILITIES
At Granville Plus Nursery School we celebrate the progress and learning of all our children. We are a highly inclusive setting with highly trained and experienced staff who have a deep understanding of child development and know exactly how to help each and every child make their next step of progress however big or small that is. We will talk to you and share what is happening at nursery for your child.
If your child needs some additional support their key person will meet with you to write a One Page Profile, which is a highly individualised document that helps us all to understand your child better and provide the most effective care and support for them. Often, we can provide all the support a child needs in nursery. But we may want to refer to specialist services to get a clearer picture or more evidence of their needs.
As a team we work alongside professionals in the NHS who carry out assessments and provide therapies for children with additional needs. Lucy (our SENDCO) can refer children in to these services. Please ask to see her if you have a concern about your child’s development.
If your child needs higher levels of support we may talk to you about a referral for additional funding. And to support them when they go to school, we may be able to help you apply for an Education, Health and Care Plan from the Local Authority.
THE LOCAL OFFER
Local Authorities and schools are required to publish and keep under review information about services they expect to be available for the children and young people with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities (SEND) aged 0-25. This is known as the ‘Local Offer’.
The intention of the Local Offer is to improve choice and transparency for families. It will also be an important resource for parents in understanding the range of services and provision in the local area. Information is published as part of the SEND reforms under the Children and Families Act 2014.
Brent Council's Local Offer can be found here:
www.brent.gov.uk/localoffer
Please contact our key SEND staff if you require any support or information about Inclusion, SEND or the Local Offer at Granville Nursery via email at admin@granvillepluscc.brent.sch.uk or call us on 0207 604 4620

Parental Involvement
We see our relationship with you as a partnership.
We aim to share our understanding of your child’s development, both informally and in other ways. We want to explore with you the ways that play encourages learning, and how we can work together on this.
You may be able to spend time :
• joining in activities - reading stories, playing turntaking games or with puzzles
• sharing an interest or skill you have, for example in dance, music, crafts, singing, woodwork, gardening, cooking, ball games
• making story props or games
• joining us on outings
We know many of you have commitments that will prevent regular helping out. We are also aware that parents feel able to become involved in many ways, which may not be directly with the children. We want all parents to feel involved.
For parents with English as an Additional Language we are happy to find interpreters, or to translate documents, where you feel this will help.

Our Curriculum Design
Planning the Curriculum
Curriculum
All learning in Granville takes place through a balance of child-led learning and more structured adult-led sessions. At this stage of development most learning takes place through child-led play-based activities which are carefully planned to target the interests of the unique child. The children are free to choose from a wide range of activities, with the staff working alongside them, to support and extend their learning.
Some of these activities will be adult-initiated, based on close observations of the children's needs and interests. Others will arise through spontaneous engagement of the children with the School’s resources, supported and extended through sensitive interaction with the staff.
Through continuous dialogue and involvement with parents, experiences at home and in School can be shared and built upon.
We cannot transmit our mature perspectives directly. However, you (as your child’s first and continuing educator) and we (as trained early years educators ) can observe, support, and extend your child’s learning.
We are very aware of the different stages of development that children go through during their time at the School. We plan the curriculum for all children to meet individual needs. We try to be very alert to the particular needs of our youngest children. We want to ensure they have as broad a range of experiences as the older children, but offered in ways appropriate to their needs and ways of learning. This is also our approach to our children with special needs.
Our curriculum is designed to support children to take risks and explore. Just learning to walk, climbing stairs, paddling in water, riding a bike or scooter carry inherent risks. Over time children will encounter increasing challenges, including with a variety of climbing equipment, building high structures with heavy blocks, and learning to handle a range of tools under appropriate supervision, such as woodwork tools and appropriately sharp knives during cooking and food preparation. Learning to identify and manage risks, alongside close and effective adult support, is a key aspect of young children's learning.
We start from where each child is - in some cases this will mean your child encountering a wide range of new experiences and resources, but if your child has already made considerable progress we aim to build on that, within a broad, balanced and creative curriculum.
“What a child can do with assistance today she will be able to do by herself tomorrow” L.S.Vygotsky
